thread:
marie: Heads up — nightly perf run shows steady memory growth with INT8 + long context (20k tokens). KV pages keep being paged in but not reclaimed, causing paging thrash and latency spikes. attaching a short profiler excerpt. :frowning:

marie: ```
[perf] epoch=3 requests=1024 longctx=20k model=redwood-7b-int8
mem_kv_total=9.8GB mem_active_slots=8.7GB evict_attempts=412 evict_success=3
page_faults/sec=190 tail_latency_p95=420ms
```

sam: Ugh. Do we have a minimal repro? Which kernel path was chosen?

marie: Repro is deterministic on pipeline-nightly branch: `./run_perf.sh --model redwood-7b --quant int8 --seq 20480 --clients 8 --profile`. Kernel selected: aten_gemm_int8_opt (see profiler).

ryan: I pulled the pprof output — looks like KV slot scan dominates CPU during eviction attempts. Flame snippet: `kv_eviction_scan -> memmove -> memset` hot. Possible metadata chasing when slots marked dirty.

anya: Also noticed slight quality drift on INT8 for >10k contexts in eval set (perp +1.8). Could be token reordering due to partial KV reuse after eviction. Not huge but correlated with warmup + eviction noise.

devon: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) our eviction heuristic uses LRU timestamp that is updated on read causing write amplification during reuse; 2) kernel choice for int8 uses page-aligned blocks that prevent compact coalescing. I'd try disabling timestamp updates on read and enable a compact-scan pass every N requests.

sam: Can we try a quick canary: change batching heuristic to prefer local KV reuse (small batches) and force fallback to bf16 kernel for longctx to compare memory patterns?

marie: Starting a canary now on canary-3 cluster with: `REDW_SERVING_PROFILE=1 REDW_KERNEL_PREFER=bf16 REDW_EVICT_COMPACT=1000 ./deploy_canary.sh canary-3`

perf-bot: Canary deployment canary-3 started at 2026-03-18T09:14:22Z. Monitoring -> https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/canary-3

ryan: Early canary logs: mem_kv_total drops to ~6.2GB, evict_attempts->evict_success ratio improves. Latency p95 down from 420ms->160ms. However batch throughput also dropped ~9% for this workload.

anya: BF16 fallback removes the int8 accuracy drift, perp delta goes to +0.2. So looks like a tradeoff: memory savings vs small quality/regression and eviction thrash.

devon: Action items: 1) marie - capture full pprof for int8/longctx and BF16 fallback (due EOD). 2) sam - prototype no-read-timestamp and compact-scan (PR). 3) ryan - run cost/latency curve for kernel selection across seq lengths. 4) anya - quantify quality delta on production eval set and determine alert thresholds. I'll sched a short sync tomorrow. :calendar:

marie: Thanks — I'll upload traces and attach links here when ready. :thumbsup:
